_metadata.filing: single, no dependents, wages only, under 65
excluded: EITC and other refundable credits (state EITCs, renter/property-tax/sales-tax/food credits, Oregon kicker)
federal tips, overtime, car-loan-interest and senior deductions (Schedule 1-A) and state counterparts
conditional deductions/credits (MA renter deduction, CT property tax credit, CA renter's credit, IN renter's deduction)
NYC/Yonkers resident tax schedules (local stands in for local taxes)
payroll taxes (FICA, CA SDI, WA Cares, MA PFML, OR transit tax) and flat per-head local levies
notes: state[i] and local[i] are dollars of tax at wage w = wageGrid.min + i * wageGrid.step; wages are treated as federal AGI.
federal.tax = 2025 single brackets (Rev. Proc. 2024-40) applied to max(0, w - 15,750) (OBBBA standard deduction); it feeds the AL, MO and OR federal-tax deductions and the NE federal-tax cap.

Taxes are computed from the rate formulas, not the official tax tables, except the Arkansas low-income table and the Wisconsin standard deduction table; formula and table differ by a few dollars at most.

local[i] = w x typical_local_income_tax_rate from the parameter file: Tax Foundation statewide average effective rates (% of AGI) for AL, IA, KY, MD, MI, MO, NY, OH, PA; population-weighted statutory county rate for IN; 0 elsewhere.

New York tax above taxable income $215,400 uses IT-201-I (2025) worksheet 8 constants ($568 recapture base, $1,831 incremental benefit), which are hard-coded in the generator rather than taken from the parameter file.

Alabama.method: AL AGI = wages; standard deduction $3,000 stepping down $25 per $500 of AGI to $2,500 (AGI $26,000-$35,500); uncapped deduction for 2025 federal income tax; $1,500 exemption; 2%/4%/5% brackets

Alaska.method: No individual income tax on wages; all zeros

Arizona.method: Wages - standard deduction - personal exemption, single-filer brackets; flat 2.5% on wages - $15,750; Family Income Tax Credit (AZ income <= $10,000) has no effect because tax is already $0 there

Arkansas.method: AGI <= $17,500: 2025 Low Income Tax Table (single); otherwise NTI = wages - $2,470 and DFA rate-minus-adjustment formulas incl. the $94,701-$97,800 recapture band and >$100k rule; minus $29 personal credit and $60-to-$0 Additional Tax Credit (NTI <= $27,600)

California.method: Wages - standard deduction - personal exemption, single-filer brackets, minus $153 exemption credit; plus $153 exemption credit; credit limitation starts above FAGI $252,203 (outside the grid); renter's credit not applied

Colorado.method: Wages - standard deduction embedded in the starting point, single-filer brackets; flat 4.4% on federal taxable income (wages - $15,750); standard-deduction add-back applies only above AGI $300,000 (outside the grid)

Connecticut.method: CT AGI = wages; $15,000 exemption phased out $1,000 per $1,000 over $30,000 (Table A); Table B schedule + 2% add-back (Table C) + recapture (Table D); times (1 - Table E personal credit decimal). Property tax credit (needs property tax paid) not applied

Delaware.method: Wages - standard deduction - personal exemption, single-filer brackets, minus $110 exemption credit; minus $110 personal credit (nonrefundable)

Florida.method: No individual income tax on wages; all zeros

Georgia.method: Wages - standard deduction - personal exemption, single-filer brackets; flat 5.19% on wages - $12,000; Low Income Credit (FAGI < $20,000) not applied because its amount table is not in the parameter file

Hawaii.method: Wages - standard deduction - personal exemption, single-filer brackets; Act 46 brackets; refundable food/excise and renter credits not applied

Idaho.method: Wages - standard deduction - personal exemption, single-filer brackets; 5.3% above a $4,811 zero band on wages - $15,750; $10 Permanent Building Fund tax and refundable Food Tax Credit not applied

Indiana.method: Wages - standard deduction - personal exemption, single-filer brackets; flat 3.0% on wages - $1,000; county tax is in 'local' (statutory rate applied to wages)

Iowa.method: Federal taxable income (wages - $15,750) x 3.8% - $40 credit; single low-income $9,000 exemption/tax reduction worksheet applied; federal Schedule 1-A deductions not applied

Kansas.method: Wages - standard deduction - personal exemption, single-filer brackets; 5.2%/5.58% on wages - $3,605 - $9,160

Kentucky.method: (Wages - $3,270) x 4%, reduced by the Family Size Tax Credit (family size 1; 100% at MGI <= $15,650 to 0% above $20,815)

Louisiana.method: Wages - standard deduction - personal exemption, single-filer brackets; flat 3% on wages - $12,500

Maine.method: Wages - standard deduction ($15,000, phased out above Maine AGI $100,000 over $75,000) - $5,150 exemption (phase-out above $333,450, outside the grid), 5.8%/6.75%/7.15% brackets

Maryland.method: Wages - $3,350 standard deduction - exemption ($3,200; $1,600 FAGI $100k-$125k; $800 to $150k; $0 above), Schedule I brackets. County tax is in 'local'

Massachusetts.method: Wages - FICA deduction (min(7.65% of wages, $2,000)) - $4,400 exemption, x 5% (9% above $1,083,150); No Tax Status at MA AGI <= $8,000; Limited Income Credit cap 10% x (MA AGI - $8,000) to $14,000. Optional renter deduction not applied

Michigan.method: Wages - standard deduction - personal exemption, single-filer brackets; flat 4.25% on wages - $5,800; city income taxes are in 'local'

Minnesota.method: Wages - $14,950 standard deduction (3%/10% phase-out above AGI $238,950), single brackets

Mississippi.method: State gross income = wages; minus standard deduction and exemption; single-filer brackets; 0% on the first $10,000 of taxable income and 4.4% above, on wages - $2,300 - $6,000

Missouri.method: MO AGI = wages; minus federal income tax deduction (35%/25%/15%/5%/0% of 2025 federal tax by MO AGI, cap $5,000) and $15,750 standard deduction; single brackets

Montana.method: Wages - standard deduction embedded in the starting point, single-filer brackets; 4.7%/5.9% on wages - $15,750

Nebraska.method: Wages - $8,600, single brackets, minus $171 exemption credit; capped at federal tax before credits (1040N line 35 limit)

Nevada.method: No individual income tax on wages; all zeros

New Hampshire.method: No individual income tax on wages; all zeros

New Jersey.method: NJ gross income = wages; no tax at or below $10,000; else (wages - $1,000) on the Table A single schedule

New Mexico.method: Wages - $15,750 federal standard deduction - low- and middle-income exemption ($2,500 less 15% of FAGI over $20,000, FAGI <= $36,667), 2025 brackets

New York.method: Wages - $8,000, NYS rate schedule; tax-benefit recapture (worksheet 7 above NY AGI $107,650; worksheet 8 above TI $215,400); minus NYS household credit (FAGI <= $28,000). NYC/Yonkers tax not applied (see 'local')

North Carolina.method: Wages - standard deduction - personal exemption, single-filer brackets; flat 4.25% on wages - $12,750

North Dakota.method: Wages - standard deduction embedded in the starting point, single-filer brackets; 0%/1.95%/2.5% on wages - $15,750

Ohio.method: Exemption $2,400/$2,150/$1,900 by MAGI; TI = wages - exemption; $0 to $26,050, $342.00 + 2.75% over $26,050, $2,394.32 + 3.125% over $100,000; minus $20 exemption credit if MAGI less exemption < $30,000

Oklahoma.method: Wages - standard deduction - personal exemption, single-filer brackets; on wages - $6,350 - $1,000; special 65+ exemption irrelevant

Oregon.method: Wages - federal income tax subtraction (cap $8,500, phased out at AGI $125k-$145k) - $2,835 standard deduction, 2025 brackets; minus $256 exemption credit only if federal AGI <= $100,000

Pennsylvania.method: Wages x 3.07%; Tax Forgiveness (Schedule SP) by eligibility income up to $8,750

Rhode Island.method: Wages - standard deduction - personal exemption, single-filer brackets; standard deduction/exemption phase-out starts above modified AGI $254,250 (outside the grid)

South Carolina.method: Wages - standard deduction embedded in the starting point, single-filer brackets; 0%/3%/6% on wages - $15,000 (SC decoupled from the $750 OBBBA increase)

South Dakota.method: No individual income tax on wages; all zeros

Tennessee.method: No individual income tax on wages; all zeros

Texas.method: No individual income tax on wages; all zeros

Utah.method: Wages x 4.5% minus taxpayer credit (6% x $15,750 = $945, less 1.3% of income over $18,213); $0 if FAGI <= $15,750

Vermont.method: Wages - $7,650 - $5,300, 2025 brackets; greater of that or 3% of FAGI when FAGI > $150,000

Virginia.method: No tax below the $11,950 VAGI filing threshold; else wages - $8,750 - $930, 2%/3%/5%/5.75% brackets

Washington.method: No individual income tax on wages; all zeros

West Virginia.method: Wages - low-income earned income exclusion (FAGI <= $10,000) - $2,000 exemption, 2025 brackets; reduced by the Family Tax Credit (family size 1, to $18,350)

Wisconsin.method: Wages - sliding standard deduction (2025 table: $13,560 less 12% of income over $19,549, evaluated at $500-row midpoints) - $700 exemption, 2025 Act 15 brackets

Wyoming.method: No individual income tax on wages; all zeros

District of Columbia.method: Wages - standard deduction - personal exemption, single-filer brackets; DC-defined $15,000 standard deduction
